cards.headline: Port St. Lucie cuts ribbon on $28.8 million police training center at City Hall
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie officially opened a 54,283-square-foot police training center on the City Hall grounds after four years of construction.
cards.body:
The $28.8 million police training center officially opened on July 24 on the grounds of Port St. Lucie City Hall with a ribbon-cutting for invited guests. The three-story facility is located just northwest of the police department. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project is about making sure officers have the space, training, and resources they need to continue serving the community at the highest level.

The facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training, a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises, and a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The facility also includes three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division, including 19 offices and 86 workstations.

Officer Brittany McNally said for years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training. By bringing much of that training in-house, the facility will reduce those recurring costs while allowing the department to train more efficiently and effectively. The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. As of July 27, the city has a population of more than 260,000 and the police department has 455 employees with 360 sworn officers.

Investigators described the home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. The house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and the home was unsafe for walking, according to Diaz. A neighbor named Suzan said she had witnessed the conditions firsthand and would see other children from the home asking for water. The children would come in the same clothes every day without bathing, she said.

Nicole Maxwell's other children who were living inside the mobile home needed medical attention at the time and are now in foster care. The Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before the infant's death. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said protecting children is a responsibility the community shares and urged residents to report signs of child abuse or neglect. The investigation took nearly a year because the medical examiner had to seek outside experts to provide an examination for the child, with results taking several weeks to months.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training center with 20-lane indoor firing range
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a three-story, 54,283-square-foot police training facility on the City Hall grounds featuring advanced virtual reality technology and indoor firearms capabilities.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie officially opened its $28.8 million police training center on July 24 with a ribbon-cutting ceremony on the City Hall grounds just northwest of the police department. The 54,283-square-foot, three-story facility was four years in construction and was designed by ADG Architecture and built by HJ High. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project ensures officers have the space, training, and resources needed to serve the community at the highest level.

The facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range with an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms, and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for decision-making and de-escalation exercises. It also features a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology, a multi-purpose training room, and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division with 19 offices and 86 workstations.

Officer Brittany McNally said the facility will reduce recurring costs from officers traveling to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for training. The new training center provides access to state-of-the-art technology and realistic scenario-based training that better prepares officers for situations they may face in the field, she said. Police personnel immediately began moving into the facility after the ribbon cutting. The facility is not open to the general public due to safety and confidentiality concerns.

cards.headline: 2 men arrested after fleeing Port St. Lucie police at 80 mph, one found hiding on occupied home's roof
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested two men after a high-speed chase ended with the suspects abandoning their car and fleeing on foot, with one hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46, were arrested after fleeing Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. Officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving, but the driver accelerated instead of pulling over. Police said the driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic and ignored traffic signs and signals before abandoning the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue.

A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash at gunpoint during Fort Pierce Wells Fargo ATM robbery
cards.teaser: Two men robbed a victim at a Fort Pierce Wells Fargo ATM, forcing him to withdraw cash before fleeing on foot Sunday night.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce became the victim of an armed robbery on Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. Two men approached the victim, and one of them displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash. The suspects fled the scene on foot.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie faces $48 million revenue loss if property tax amendment passes in November
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie is deferring projects and freezing 184 positions, including 25 new police officers, as the city prepares for a potential $48 million property tax revenue loss if Amendment 3 passes.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if Amendment 3 passes on the November 3 ballot, City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council during a summer budget workshop at the Port St. Lucie Community Center on Thursday. The city is not funding 184 requested positions worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff planned to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park.

The city has canceled $7.8 million in projects including a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, and construction on a new City Hall and parking garage. City employees will not receive a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said costs continually rise and the only place to take reductions from is personnel, meaning the department will have to reduce its size.

Amendment 3 would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028. The constitutional amendment needs at least 60% approval from voters to pass. Scott Samples with the city said the council will reconvene shortly after the November 3 election to determine next steps. St. Lucie County homeowners currently pay the highest property tax in the state, according to Florida tax data.
cards.article_text: Lucie review the upcoming city budget as some city council members worry about lost revenue if property taxes go away. Lucie hosted the summer budget workshop at the Port St. Lucie Community Center Thursday morning. During the workshop, City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if the item passes in November. To prepare for the potential hit, the city isn't just deferring projects it's also holding the line on hiring. Lucie says it won't fund 184 requested positions, worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. Well, our costs continually rise just like everybody else. So, the only place that we can take that from is personnel. So, we'll have to reduce the size of the place, said Police Chief Leo Niemczyk when asked how this budget will impact the department. See also: Funeral held for Belle Glade father, two sons killed when pickup overturned into canal City employees also won't get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. On the capital side, the $7.8 million in canceled projects includes a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage Despite parks and recreation receiving an extra $1.34 million, most of that money is tied to new developments, such as the Torino Regional Park and the BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. Parks and recreation officials told city councilors what a lack of new staff to keep these parks going will look like. I dare say the dirty words of deferred maintenance. But that's the reality when you don't have the people in the parks to maintain them at the level that we've been accustomed to doing, said Brad Keen, the director of the parks and recreation department. Not everything is being cut, though. The police department's budget is actually going up nearly 10%, to just under $104 million, driven mostly by a 5% contractual raise for sworn officers along with new equipment, training and technology upgrades. But the number of officers isn't growing; staffing stays flat at just over 468 positions, meaning the department is spending more to keep the officers it already has, not to add more. City leaders have flagged public safety, police, code enforcement, and emergency management as the areas most exposed if deeper cuts are eventually needed, since they already eat up 56% of the city's general fund. This is the reality of what the future is for, not just our city, but all this needs for safety if we're not able to be competitive and keep our officers, said Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo. The proposal, known as Amendment 3, is headed to Florida voters on the November 3, 2026 ballot after the Legislature passed it during a June special session. If approved, it would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028, while also directing lawmakers to come up with a plan to eliminate non-school property taxes on homesteaded properties eventually. Because it's a constitutional amendment, it needs at least 60% approval from voters to pass. Economists have estimated the change could cut local government revenue statewide by billions of dollars a year, which is why cities and counties across Florida, including Port St. Lucie, are already building the potential loss into their budget planning. Lucie County homeowners currently pay the highest property tax in the state, according to Florida tax data. Scott Samples with the city said the council will reconvene shortly after the November 3rd election to determine next steps, whether the proposal is passed or fails.

cards.headline: P1 Motor Club building private racetrack resort community in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: A new private racetrack resort community featuring 10 miles of racing circuits is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, with the first track opening in October.
cards.body:
P1 Motor Club is being built on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road in St. Lucie County, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, described it as a high-end golf resort with a racetrack instead of a golf course.

The club is designed for drivers of all ages and skill levels, with kids as young as 8 years old driving go-karts. Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members. Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks.

Developers say they want to preserve the character of the region by planting trees, creating lakes, and incorporating natural landscaping throughout the property. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County corrections deputy sentenced to probation after road rage incident in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Devin Mills, a St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office corrections deputy, was sentenced to two years of probation after pleading no contest to burglary charges related to an off-duty road rage incident.
cards.body:
Devin Mills, 57, a St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office corrections deputy, was sentenced on July 16 to two years of probation and must pay court costs after pleading no contest to a burglary of a conveyance charge on June 29. Florida Department of Corrections records indicate Mills' probation is supervised by its Fort Pierce Circuit office and expires on July 15, 2028. Court documents note the probation will automatically terminate after one year if he completes conditions including a mental health evaluation and if needed, treatment, along with no contact with the victims or victims' families.

Mills was accused of confronting two 18-year-olds in a vehicle during a road rage incident on the 100 block of SW Tulip Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. A video recording by the teenagers showed Mills reaching into the open passenger-side of the teens' vehicle, grabbing one of the teens' arms to take the cellphone that was recording the incident away.

A spokesperson for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office told WPBF 25 News on July 23 that Mills' employment status is pending the completion of an internal affairs investigation. After his no-contest plea, the Sheriff's Office said Mills remained on unpaid administrative leave pending an internal investigation.

hero.headline: Cyclist rides through Vero Beach on 2,600-mile journey from Key West to Maine
hero.teaser: A Boston cyclist rode through Vero Beach this week on a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine to honor a friend lost to colorectal cancer.
hero.body:
Jay Weedall traveled to South Florida to begin the journey, with a goal of raising $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center. Weedall began his journey in Key West, pedaling 155 miles to Miami on day one. He set off on his second leg, a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach, after filling his hydration pack with ice to stay cool.

Weedall is riding roughly 150 miles a day up the coast through nearly every state all the way to the Pan Mass Challenge. He will do the Pan Mass Challenge across Massachusetts on August 2 and continue to the Canadian border in Maine. By avoiding highways, Weedall says the route offers something unexpected, allowing him to experience little coastal towns along the inlets. Fans can follow Weedall's journey on the cycling app Strava.
hero.article_text: A Boston cyclist is turning heartbreak into hope. After losing a close friend to young-onset colorectal cancer, Jay Weedall traveled to South Florida to begin a 2,600-mile bike ride from Key West to Maine, with a goal of raising $50,000 for research while honoring his friend's memory.WATCH BELOW:"A friend of mine recently passed away from young onset rectal cancer," Weedall said.The death of his friend, who was also named Jay, inspired Weedall to honor his memory by riding his bike across the country."I've adventured around the world with him, ridden bikes together with him, and this felt like the best way to honor him now that he's passed away," Weedall said.His goal is to raise $50,000 for the Young Onset Colorectal Cancer Research Center in honor of the friend he lost to the disease. To prepare, Weedall trained 200 to 300 miles a week, mapped out his route, and planned for the long journey ahead."So, there was a lot of preplanning to make sure that the roads that I'm going to go on are safe and have been ridden on by cyclists and let's hope that the wind is kind to me," Weedall said.Weedall began his journey in Key West, pedaling 155 miles to Miami on day one."Something I learned after day one is hydration packs, good for hydration obviously but if you fill it up with ice it's good for keeping you cold as well," Weedall said.I caught up with him the next morning as he set off on his second leg — a 163-mile ride to Vero Beach."Ideally, I try to beat the heat and then I'm going roughly 150 miles a day just niching my way up the coast through pretty much every state all the way to the Pan Mass Challenge. hero.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce became the victim of an armed robbery Sunday night when two men forced him to withdraw cash before fleeing on foot. The Fort Pierce Police Department reported the incident occurred at approximately 8:38 p.m.

Two men approached the victim while he was at the ATM. One of the suspects displayed a gun that was concealed in his waistband and forced the victim to withdraw cash. The amount of money taken remains unknown. After obtaining the cash, both suspects fled the scene on foot.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the robbery and established a perimeter around the area. Law enforcement deployed both a K-9 unit and a drone to search for the suspects. Despite these efforts, the suspects were not located.

Police described both suspects as men in their early 20s, standing approximately 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing around 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt. The Fort Pierce Police Department is investigating the incident.

cards.headline: Three arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce home
cards.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in a Fort Pierce mobile home. Nicole Maxwell, Robert Maxwell, and Vikki Koon were arrested Monday, nearly a year after the infant died at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in August 2025.

The investigation began when Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the deceased infant to the hospital on Aug. 20, 2025. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition and ruled the death a homicide. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Vikki Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with baby cereal mixed in.

The child lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon while Nicole Maxwell, the infant's mother, lived at her boyfriend's home in Vero Beach. Investigators described the mobile home as having windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. Detective Jennifer Diaz said the house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and was unsafe for walking. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the conditions and would see other children from the home asking for water. The children appeared unbathed and wore the same clothes every day, she said.

Nicole Maxwell's four other children who were living in the mobile home are now in foster care. The Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before the infant's death. Detective Diaz, who has 20 years in law enforcement, called it one of the worst cases she has ever worked. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said protecting children is a responsibility the community shares and urged residents to report signs of child abuse or neglect.

cards.headline: Suspect found hiding on roof after 80 mph chase through Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: A suspected drunk driver and his passenger fled Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph before abandoning their car and running, with one suspect later found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving. The driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. The driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic, ignored traffic signs and signals, then abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot.

A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home. Joseph Gary Harris, 42, was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Bryan Shawn Baker, 46, was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training center at City Hall
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center that includes a 20-lane indoor firearms range and tactical shoot house after four years of construction.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie officials cut the ribbon Thursday on a $28.8 million police training center on the City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. The 54,283-square-foot facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training, and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises.

The three-story facility also includes a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology, a multi-purpose training room, and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division with 19 offices and 86 workstations. The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. For years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training. Officer Brittany McNally said bringing training in-house will reduce recurring costs while allowing officers to train more efficiently and effectively.
cards.article_text: The recently opened Port St. Lucie Police training center contains a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The recently opened, 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center is on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. The 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center officially opened on July 24 on the grounds of Port St. Lucie City Hall with a ribbon-cutting for invited guests. The interior of the 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. Lucie city officials who cut the ribbon for the 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center on July 24 were Mayor Shannon Martin, center, and Chief Leo Niemczyk. LUCIE – After four years of construction, the ribbon was cut on July 24 for a 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. “This project is all about making sure our officers have the space, training, and resources they need to continue serving our community at the highest level,” Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin said in a Facebook posting. Lucie the safest large city in Florida takes more than dedication. It requires planning ahead and making smart investments that prepare our officers for the challenges they face every day.” Included in the three-story facility are: • A 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system. • A 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training. • A MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. • A dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. • A multi-purpose training room designed for classroom instruction, conferences, virtual presentations, and large-scale training. • Three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division (CID), including 19 offices and 86 workstations. • Advanced audio/visual technology throughout the facility to support collaborative training and instruction. The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High, with specialized contributions from industry leaders including Action Target, MILO, Whelen, and numerous additional project partners, according to Port St. As of July 27, the city has a population of more than 260,000. There is a total of 455 employees in the police department with 360 sworn officers, according to city hall records. For years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training, according to Officer Brittany McNally. “By bringing much of that training in-house, this facility will reduce those recurring costs while allowing us to train more efficiently and effectively,” she said in a statement. “Equally important, the new training facility provides our officers with access to state-of-the-art technology and realistic, scenario-based training that better prepares them for the complex situations they may face in the field. From recruit training to advanced tactical instruction and continuing education, our officers will now have the resources needed to sharpen their skills throughout their careers right in our own backyard.” Once the ribbon was cut, police personnel immediately began making the move into the new facility. cards.headline: Big Taste of Martin County fundraiser set for October in Stuart
cards.teaser: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold Big Taste of Martin County on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart to fund mentoring programs for children.
cards.body:
Big Brothers Big Sisters of Palm Beach and Martin Counties will hold Big Taste of Martin County on Oct. 6 at Atlantic Aviation in Stuart. The food and spirits event brings together local restaurants, chefs and community partners to support mentoring programs for children across the Treasure Coast.

Guests can sample food, wine and beer from area businesses while participating restaurants compete for Big Taste awards. The event helps fund mentorship opportunities for children who are waiting to be matched with a mentor.

Spritz Stuart plans to feature several menu items during the event including a Tuscan salmon dish, a smash burger and a specialty cocktail called the Fig & Flame. Community members can support the mission by purchasing tickets, attending the event or volunteering to become a mentor.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Museum of Art to hold Second Saturday program Aug. 8 with recycled fishing line bracelets
cards.teaser: The Vero Beach Museum of Art and Coastal Connections will team up for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8 with hands-on activities and gallery tours.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach Museum of Art and Coastal Connections will hold a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. Aug. 8 at the museum at 3001 Riverside Drive in Vero Beach. Activities include hands-on projects, gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life.

Coastal Connections will lead an activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways. Participants also can learn about the Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp.

Families can take short docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can then participate in Nature in Layers, an art activity for children connected to the museum's exhibitions. Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day.
cards.article_text: Recycled fishing line is transformed into a friendship bracelet during a hands-on activity presented by Coastal Connections at the Vero Beach Museum of Art. VERO BEACH — Discarded fishing line will find new purpose as friendship bracelets when art and marine conservation come together at the Vero Beach Museum of Art. The museum and Coastal Connections will team up for a free Second Saturday program beginning at 10 a.m. 8, with hands-on activities, gallery tours and lessons about protecting local marine life. Activities also include docent-led mini-tours, studio art projects and opportunities to learn about protecting local marine life. Coastal Connections will lead a hands-on activity in the Laura and Bill Buck Atrium, where visitors can make friendship bracelets using recycled fishing line collected from local waterways. Participants also can learn about the organization’s Fishing Line Recycling Program. The museum has adopted the fishing line recycling tube at the Riverside Park boat ramp. to 1 p.m., families can take short, docent-led gallery tours through the Museum Studios family program. Visitors can then participate in “Nature in Layers,” an art activity for children connected to the museum’s exhibitions. Guests also can tour the museum’s summer exhibitions throughout the day. “James Prosek: At Work” is on view in the Holmes Gallery, while “Jill Nathanson: Chromatic Phrases” is displayed in the Schumann and Titelman galleries. “Our partnership with VBMA is a great example of how we are working with our community to introduce everyone to marine conservation and environmental protection in unique ways,” explained Kendra Bergman, founder and executive director of Coastal Connections. “Collaborations like these are key to meeting our mission and watching one of the greatest conservation success stories unfold within our lifetime.” Second Saturday includes free museum admission throughout the day. Additional programs may include performances, lectures, films and other arts and humanities offerings on select Saturdays. Coastal Connections was founded in 2017 with a mission of advancing the survival of sea turtles by educating and connecting people to the environment. hero.headline: 3 arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce
hero.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old died from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce. Nicole Maxwell, the infant's mother, Robert Maxwell, the grandfather, and Vikki Koon, the grandfather's girlfriend, were arrested Monday by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Detective Jennifer Diaz said the case is one of the worst she has encountered in 20 years of law enforcement.

The investigation began in August 2025 when investigators responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the 3-month-old in deceased. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. The child lived primarily with Maxwell and Koon while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home. Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with bay cereal mixed in.

Investigators found the mobile home where the infant lived had windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring and live and dead cockroaches throughout. The house was extremely hot with a bug infestation and was unsafe for walking, according to Diaz. A neighbor named Suzan said she witnessed the conditions firsthand and described the home as unlivable. She said other children would come to her door asking for water and appeared thirsty and unwashed, wearing the same clothes every day.

Nicole Maxwell's other children who were living inside the mobile home are now in foster care. The Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before. Sheriff Richard Del Toro released a statement urging the public to report any signs that a child may be neglected, abused or living in unsafe conditions. Diaz emphasized that tips are instrumental to keeping children safe.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie cuts 184 planned positions from budget to prepare for possible property tax elimination
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie is deferring 184 requested positions worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers, as the city prepares for a potential $48 million loss in property tax revenue.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie will not fund 184 requested positions worth $28.3 million as the city prepares for potential lost revenue if a property tax elimination amendment passes in November. The unfunded positions include 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council during a summer budget workshop Thursday that the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if the item passes.

The city is also canceling $7.8 million in capital projects, including a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage. City employees will not get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said the department would have to reduce the size of its staff as costs rise.

Amendment 3 is headed to Florida voters on November 3, 2026 after the Legislature passed it during a June special session. If approved with at least 60 percent voter support, it would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028. The city council will reconvene shortly after the November 3 election to determine next steps.
cards.article_text: Lucie review the upcoming city budget as some city council members worry about lost revenue if property taxes go away. Lucie hosted the summer budget workshop at the Port St. Lucie Community Center Thursday morning. During the workshop, City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if the item passes in November. To prepare for the potential hit, the city isn't just deferring projects it's also holding the line on hiring. Lucie says it won't fund 184 requested positions, worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. Well, our costs continually rise just like everybody else. So, the only place that we can take that from is personnel. So, we'll have to reduce the size of the place, said Police Chief Leo Niemczyk when asked how this budget will impact the department. See also: Funeral held for Belle Glade father, two sons killed when pickup overturned into canal City employees also won't get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. On the capital side, the $7.8 million in canceled projects includes a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage Despite parks and recreation receiving an extra $1.34 million, most of that money is tied to new developments, such as the Torino Regional Park and the BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. Parks and recreation officials told city councilors what a lack of new staff to keep these parks going will look like. I dare say the dirty words of deferred maintenance. But that's the reality when you don't have the people in the parks to maintain them at the level that we've been accustomed to doing, said Brad Keen, the director of the parks and recreation department. Not everything is being cut, though. The police department's budget is actually going up nearly 10%, to just under $104 million, driven mostly by a 5% contractual raise for sworn officers along with new equipment, training and technology upgrades. But the number of officers isn't growing; staffing stays flat at just over 468 positions, meaning the department is spending more to keep the officers it already has, not to add more. City leaders have flagged public safety, police, code enforcement, and emergency management as the areas most exposed if deeper cuts are eventually needed, since they already eat up 56% of the city's general fund. This is the reality of what the future is for, not just our city, but all this needs for safety if we're not able to be competitive and keep our officers, said Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo. The proposal, known as Amendment 3, is headed to Florida voters on the November 3, 2026 ballot after the Legislature passed it during a June special session. If approved, it would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028, while also directing lawmakers to come up with a plan to eliminate non-school property taxes on homesteaded properties eventually. Because it's a constitutional amendment, it needs at least 60% approval from voters to pass. Economists have estimated the change could cut local government revenue statewide by billions of dollars a year, which is why cities and counties across Florida, including Port St. Lucie, are already building the potential loss into their budget planning. Lucie County homeowners currently pay the highest property tax in the state, according to Florida tax data. Scott Samples with the city said the council will reconvene shortly after the November 3rd election to determine next steps, whether the proposal is passed or fails.

cards.headline: Man forced to withdraw cash at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce during armed robbery
cards.teaser: Two men approached a victim at a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce Sunday night, with one displaying a gun before forcing the victim to withdraw cash.
cards.body:
A man using a Wells Fargo ATM became the victim of an armed robbery after two men forced him to pull out cash before fleeing the scene on foot Sunday at about 8:38 p.m. One of the men displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw an unknown amount of cash, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the scene, established a perimeter, and used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects. The suspects were not located. Police described them as two men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police open $28.8 million training facility with indoor firing range and tactical shoot house
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a 54,283-square-foot police training center on July 24 after four years of construction.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie opened a 54,283-square-foot, $28.8 million police training center on July 24 on the grounds of City Hall, just northwest of the police department. The three-story facility includes a 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system, a 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training, and a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. The center also features a dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology and three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division.

The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. For years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training, according to Officer Brittany McNally. By bringing much of that training in-house, the facility will reduce those recurring costs while allowing the department to train more efficiently and effectively, she said.

Port St. Lucie has a population of more than 260,000 as of July 27. The police department has a total of 455 employees with 360 sworn officers. Mayor Shannon Martin said the project is about making sure officers have the space, training and resources they need to continue serving the community at the highest level.

cards.headline: 2 men arrested after high-speed chase in Port St. Lucie, one found hiding on roof of occupied home
cards.teaser: Joseph Gary Harris and Bryan Shawn Baker fled from Port St. Lucie police at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before abandoning their car and running.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested two men after a suspected drunk driver fled officers at nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone before he and his passenger abandoned their car and ran, with one suspect later found hiding on the roof of an occupied home. Officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road.

The driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic, ignored traffic signs and signals, then abandoned the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue before fleeing on foot. A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter.

The suspects were identified as Joseph Gary Harris, 42, and Bryan Shawn Baker, 46. Harris was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Baker was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: P1 Motor Club building private racetrack resort community on 650 acres in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: P1 Motor Club is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts.
cards.body:
A new private racetrack resort community is under construction in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and welcoming its first drivers this fall. P1 Motor Club is being built on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, described it as a high-end golf resort with a racetrack instead of a golf course.

The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members.

Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County corrections deputy sentenced to probation after off-duty road rage incident in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Devin Mills, a 57-year-old St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office corrections deputy, was sentenced to two years of probation after pleading no contest to burglary of a conveyance.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office corrections deputy was sentenced July 16 to two years of probation after an off-duty physical road rage incident. Devin Mills, 57, pleaded no contest to burglary of a conveyance charge on June 29 and must pay court costs. Florida Department of Corrections database records indicate Mills' probation is supervised by its Fort Pierce Circuit office and expires on July 15, 2028.

Court documents state Mills' probation will automatically terminate after one year if he completes conditions of probation, which include a mental health evaluation and if needed, treatment, along with no contact with the victims or victims families during the probation. Mills was accused of confronting two 18-year-olds in a vehicle during a road rage incident on the 100 block of SW Tulip Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. A video recording by the teenagers showed Mills reaching into the open passenger-side of the teens vehicle and grabbing one of the teens arms to take the cellphone that was recording the incident away.

After his no-contest plea, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Mills remained on unpaid administrative leave pending an internal investigation. A spokesperson for the sheriff's office said on July 23 that Mills' employment status is pending the completion of an internal affairs investigation.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets return to Clover Park for seven-game homestand against Fort Myers
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets return to Clover Park for a seven-game series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels from Tuesday through Sunday. Tuesday's game starts at 6:05 p.m., Wednesday features a summer camp day with an 11:10 a.m. start, and Thursday includes a doubleheader beginning at 4:00 p.m. The doubleheader is part of a makeup game from a June 27 rainout in Fort Myers. Friday and Saturday games start at 6:10 p.m., and Sunday's finale is scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Thursday's doubleheader will feature Paint the Park Pink for breast cancer awareness, with the Mets wearing special pink jerseys that fans can bid on through July 29 at stluciemets.com/auction. A breast cancer survivor and fighter parade will take place on the field between games. Saturday is Maddie's Fight Night with postgame fireworks, with the Mets wearing special autographed jerseys that will be auctioned off with all proceeds going to Maddie's Fight Foundation, a 501c3 that helps families with children undergoing cancer treatment.

Promotions throughout the week include Silver Sluggers Night on Tuesday, with members receiving admission, parking, and a hot dog. Wednesday is Baseball Bingo and camp day for summer camps from around the Treasure Coast. Thursday also features $2 Night with discounts on Bud Light, Budweiser, Busch Light, hot dogs, fountain sodas, and popcorn. Friday includes Vets at the Mets, with all veterans and active duty military receiving free admission courtesy of LYNQ Real Estate, and Joe Torre Safe At Home Night with custom Topps cards.

Tickets to all games are available at www.stluciemets.com or at the box office. The Amazin Mets Foundation 50/50 Charity Raffle will run from 10 a.m. Tuesday through the seventh inning of Sunday's game, with half the pot going to the winner and the other half to Graceway Village. Anyone within Florida can purchase raffle tickets at stluciemets.com/5050.

hero.headline: Three arrested in St. Lucie County after 3-month-old dies from dehydration and malnutrition
hero.body:
Three people face charges of aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse after a 3-month-old infant died from dehydration and malnutrition in Fort Pierce. Nicole Maxwell, the infant's mother, Robert Maxwell, the grandfather, and Vikki Koon, the grandfather's girlfriend, were arrested Monday following an investigation that began in August 2025.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office responded to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital after Robert Maxwell and Koon brought the infant in deceased. The medical examiner determined the child died from dehydration and malnutrition. Court documents describe the infant's ribs as more prominent than its stomach. Detective Jennifer Diaz called it one of the worst cases in her 20 years of law enforcement.

The infant lived primarily with Robert Maxwell and Koon in a mobile home while Nicole Maxwell lived at her boyfriend's home. Koon told investigators she fed the infant only twice a day and when she ran out of formula, she fed the child watered-down milk with bay cereal mixed in. The home had windows boarded shut, exposed electrical wiring, and live and dead cockroaches throughout. A neighbor named Suzan witnessed the conditions and said children from the home would knock on her door asking for water.

Nicole Maxwell's other children who were living in the mobile home are now in foster care. The Department of Children and Families had been involved with the family before the infant's death. Sheriff Richard Del Toro urged community members to report signs of child abuse or neglect, stating that one phone call can be the difference between a child receiving help and a life being saved.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie opens $28.8 million police training facility with indoor firearms range
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie cut the ribbon on a three-story, 54,283-square-foot police training center on the City Hall grounds after four years of construction.
cards.body:
The training center officially opened July 24 and includes a 20-lane indoor firearms range, a tactical shoot house with configurable rooms, a MILO Virtual Simulation Theater, and a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The facility also features three floors of office space for the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division, including 19 offices and 86 workstations.

The new facility allows officers to train in-house instead of traveling to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training. Officer Brittany McNally said the change will reduce recurring costs while allowing more efficient training. The facility includes advanced audio and visual technology throughout to support collaborative training and instruction.

The building was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High. Port St. Lucie has a population of more than 260,000 and the police department employs 455 people with 360 sworn officers. The facility is not open to the general public due to safety and confidentiality concerns.
cards.article_text: The recently opened Port St. Lucie Police training center contains a defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. The recently opened, 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center is on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. The 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center officially opened on July 24 on the grounds of Port St. Lucie City Hall with a ribbon-cutting for invited guests. The interior of the 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. Lucie city officials who cut the ribbon for the 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center on July 24 were Mayor Shannon Martin, center, and Chief Leo Niemczyk. LUCIE – After four years of construction, the ribbon was cut on July 24 for a 54,283-square-foot, state-of-the-art, $28.8 million police training center on the Port St. Lucie City Hall grounds, just northwest of the police department. “This project is all about making sure our officers have the space, training, and resources they need to continue serving our community at the highest level,” Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin said in a Facebook posting. Lucie the safest large city in Florida takes more than dedication. It requires planning ahead and making smart investments that prepare our officers for the challenges they face every day.” Included in the three-story facility are: • A 20-lane, 9,508-square-foot indoor firearms range featuring an integrated MILO live-fire scenario system. • A 2,848-square-foot tactical shoot house with configurable rooms for realistic scenario-based training. • A MILO Virtual Simulation Theater for immersive decision-making and de-escalation exercises. • A dedicated defensive tactics training room equipped with Axon VR technology. • A multi-purpose training room designed for classroom instruction, conferences, virtual presentations, and large-scale training. • Three floors of office space supporting the Training Division and Criminal Investigations Division (CID), including 19 offices and 86 workstations. • Advanced audio/visual technology throughout the facility to support collaborative training and instruction. The facility was designed by ADG Architecture and constructed by HJ High, with specialized contributions from industry leaders including Action Target, MILO, Whelen, and numerous additional project partners, according to Port St. As of July 27, the city has a population of more than 260,000. There is a total of 455 employees in the police department with 360 sworn officers, according to city hall records. For years, officers traveled to Indian River State College in Fort Pierce for extensive training, according to Officer Brittany McNally. “By bringing much of that training in-house, this facility will reduce those recurring costs while allowing us to train more efficiently and effectively,” she said in a statement. “Equally important, the new training facility provides our officers with access to state-of-the-art technology and realistic, scenario-based training that better prepares them for the complex situations they may face in the field. From recruit training to advanced tactical instruction and continuing education, our officers will now have the resources needed to sharpen their skills throughout their careers right in our own backyard.” Once the ribbon was cut, police personnel immediately began making the move into the new facility. cards.headline: Armed robbery at Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce forces victim to withdraw cash
cards.teaser: Two men forced a victim to withdraw cash from a Wells Fargo ATM in Fort Pierce on Sunday night before fleeing on foot.
cards.body:
The robbery occurred at about 8:38 p.m. Sunday when two men approached the victim at the ATM. One of the suspects displayed a gun concealed in his waistband before forcing the victim to withdraw cash. The suspects then fled on foot.

Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department responded and established a perimeter. Police used a K-9 and drone to search for the suspects but did not locate them. Police described both suspects as men in their early 20s, about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighing about 170 pounds. The armed suspect was last seen wearing jeans and a gray hooded sweatshirt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie bans gas station on Tradition commercial parcel after neighborhood opposition
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council permanently prohibited a gas station from being built on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive.
cards.body:
The council unanimously approved the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development on July 13. The amendment changes the parcel's designation from residential to commercial while codifying a restriction that bars any current or future owner from developing a service station on the site.

Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission to convert what had been planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development into commercial property. Several Heritage Oaks residents urged the council to reject the land-use change, citing concerns about increased traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts. The council initially tabled the request in May to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use.

Before any mass grading begins, the developer must install a fence along the southern property line to prevent construction access through Southwest Glenbrook Drive. An architectural wall and landscape buffering must be completed along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued for vertical construction. Councilman Anthony Bonna said expanding commercial development will benefit residents by broadening the city's tax base.
cards.article_text: The aerial view of the 9.4-acre parcel of the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Port St. The land-use map of the 9.4-acre parcel of the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive in Port St. LUCIE — After months of debate and neighborhood concerns, the Port St. Lucie City Council has permanently prohibited a gas station from being built on a 9.4-acre commercial parcel at the southwest corner of Crosstown Parkway and Fairgreen Drive. The council unanimously approved the second and final reading of the 16th amendment to the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development on July 13, codifying a restriction that bars any current or future owner from developing a service station on the site. The amendment changes the parcel’s designation from residential to commercial, paving the way for retail and office development while addressing residents’ concerns about traffic and congestion. The issue has been under discussion for nearly three months after Winding River Crosstown LLC requested permission to convert what had been planned as Phase 3 of the Heritage Oaks at Tradition residential development into commercial property. While council members generally supported adding commercial uses to the rapidly growing area, several voiced concerns during the initial May 26 quasi-judicial hearing that a convenience store with gas pumps would worsen traffic along Crosstown Parkway west of Interstate 95. Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo and other council members noted the increasing congestion along the commercial corridor and asked staff to determine whether gas stations could be eliminated as a permitted use on the parcel. The council tabled the request to allow time for that review. At the time, Councilwoman Stephanie Morgan questioned whether prohibiting a specific type of business amounted to government interference in the marketplace. “What concerns me is that on May 11 we approved two parcels changing from RGC to commercial general,” Morgan said during the May hearing. “We didn’t put any conditions on them. How can you put a condition on an applicant saying no gas stations? That would be like saying no Chick-fil-A because we’ve got enough chicken restaurants.” When the hearing resumed June 22, several Heritage Oaks residents urged the council to reject the land-use change, citing concerns about increased traffic, noise and neighborhood impacts. Instead, the council voted 4-0, with Morgan absent, to approve the commercial designation on first reading after the developer agreed to permanently relinquish the right to build a gas station. During the July 13 meeting, city planner Bridget Kean outlined the changes that formally incorporated the restriction into the Tradition MPUD documents. The updated development plan specifies that while service stations remain a permitted use elsewhere within the mixed-use area, they are prohibited on Parcel 11A. The concept plan also now includes a notation prohibiting a service station on the property, and the ordinance itself was revised to reference the city’s definition of a service station. Staff also added additional protections requested by nearby residents. Before any mass grading begins, the developer must install a fence along the southern property line to prevent construction access through Southwest Glenbrook Drive, which connects to Heritage Oaks. In addition, an architectural wall and landscape buffering must be completed along the southeastern and southern boundaries before the first building permit is issued for vertical construction. Several residents again voiced concerns about the proposal and questioned whether the process had been sufficiently transparent. Councilman Anthony Bonna defended both the public process and the final compromise. “Ultimately, we have to make decisions, and those decisions are not going to satisfy everybody,” Bonna said. “We listen and consider every resident that comes forward, but ultimately we have to make one decision.” Bonna said he believes expanding commercial development will benefit residents by broadening the city’s tax base. Lucie has long lacked commercial, which is a burden on homeowners,” he said. “We have had several hearings here at the city, so that is what transparency is: open meetings where people can come and share their opinions and be a part of the process.” Councilman David Pickett agreed, saying the city has consistently heard residents oppose additional housing. “When this was first introduced, I was very excited that they wanted to go from residential to commercial,” Pickett said. “It doesn’t matter which way we rule, there’s always going to be somebody in opposition. For me, going to commercial is the best possible thing for that corner.” Morgan, who had questioned the gas station restriction during the first hearing, ultimately supported the ordinance. “We have heard from so many community residents — no more housetops,” she said. “It has been transparent, there’s no denying that.” Before the vote, Mayor Shannon Martin asked staff to confirm that the prohibition would remain with the property regardless of ownership. Kean confirmed the restriction is now written directly into the Tradition MPUD documents, ensuring no future owner can develop a gas station on the parcel. The council then voted unanimously to approve the ordinance, ending months of discussion and clearing the way for commercial development while permanently removing a gas station as a future possibility. cards.headline: Two men arrested after fleeing Port St. Lucie police at 80 mph, one found hiding on roof
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested two men after a high-speed chase ended with the suspects abandoning their car and fleeing on foot, with one found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.
cards.body:
Officers attempted to stop a white Acura after observing multiple traffic violations and signs of impaired driving. The driver accelerated to nearly 80 mph in a 45 mph zone on Southwest Becker Road. The driver and passenger weaved in and out of traffic and ignored traffic signs and signals before abandoning the vehicle in a residential driveway near Southwest Idol Avenue.

A nearby resident called 911 after seeing the two men run from the scene. Police deployed a K-9 and a drone while officers established a perimeter. Both suspects were located, including one who was found hiding on the roof of an occupied home.

Joseph Gary Harris, 42, was charged with fleeing and eluding law enforcement, burglary of an occupied dwelling, resisting an officer without violence, and loitering or prowling. Bryan Shawn Baker, 46, was charged with resisting an officer without violence and loitering or prowling.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie faces $48 million budget hit if property tax amendment passes
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if a constitutional amendment passes in November, prompting the city to defer projects and freeze hiring.
cards.body:
City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council during a summer budget workshop on July 23 that the city is preparing for the potential hit by holding the line on hiring. Port St. Lucie will not fund 184 requested positions worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff planned to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. City employees will not receive a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget.

The city canceled $7.8 million in projects, including a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park. Construction on a new City Hall and parking garage was also canceled. The police department's budget is increasing nearly 10 percent to just under $104 million, driven mostly by a 5 percent contractual raise for sworn officers, but staffing stays flat at just over 468 positions.

Amendment 3 would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027 and to $250,000 in January 2028. The constitutional amendment needs at least 60 percent approval from voters to pass in the November 3 election. Scott Samples with the city said the council will reconvene shortly after the election to determine next steps.
cards.article_text: Lucie review the upcoming city budget as some city council members worry about lost revenue if property taxes go away. Lucie hosted the summer budget workshop at the Port St. Lucie Community Center Thursday morning. During the workshop, City Manager Jesus Merejo told the City Council the city would lose over $48 million in property taxes over the next two years if the item passes in November. To prepare for the potential hit, the city isn't just deferring projects it's also holding the line on hiring. Lucie says it won't fund 184 requested positions, worth $28.3 million, including 25 new police officers and parks staff the city had already planned to add this year to keep up with growth at Torino Regional Park and the new BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. Well, our costs continually rise just like everybody else. So, the only place that we can take that from is personnel. So, we'll have to reduce the size of the place, said Police Chief Leo Niemczyk when asked how this budget will impact the department. See also: Funeral held for Belle Glade father, two sons killed when pickup overturned into canal City employees also won't get a cost-of-living raise in the coming budget. On the capital side, the $7.8 million in canceled projects includes a study for a new interchange connecting Marshall Parkway to I-95, an inclusive playground at McChesney Park, and parking improvements at Riverland Paseo Park, along with construction on a new City Hall and parking garage Despite parks and recreation receiving an extra $1.34 million, most of that money is tied to new developments, such as the Torino Regional Park and the BMX facility at Tradition Regional Park. Parks and recreation officials told city councilors what a lack of new staff to keep these parks going will look like. I dare say the dirty words of deferred maintenance. But that's the reality when you don't have the people in the parks to maintain them at the level that we've been accustomed to doing, said Brad Keen, the director of the parks and recreation department. Not everything is being cut, though. The police department's budget is actually going up nearly 10%, to just under $104 million, driven mostly by a 5% contractual raise for sworn officers along with new equipment, training and technology upgrades. But the number of officers isn't growing; staffing stays flat at just over 468 positions, meaning the department is spending more to keep the officers it already has, not to add more. City leaders have flagged public safety, police, code enforcement, and emergency management as the areas most exposed if deeper cuts are eventually needed, since they already eat up 56% of the city's general fund. This is the reality of what the future is for, not just our city, but all this needs for safety if we're not able to be competitive and keep our officers, said Vice Mayor Jolien Caraballo. The proposal, known as Amendment 3, is headed to Florida voters on the November 3, 2026 ballot after the Legislature passed it during a June special session. If approved, it would raise the state's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 starting in January 2027, and to $250,000 in January 2028, while also directing lawmakers to come up with a plan to eliminate non-school property taxes on homesteaded properties eventually. Because it's a constitutional amendment, it needs at least 60% approval from voters to pass. Economists have estimated the change could cut local government revenue statewide by billions of dollars a year, which is why cities and counties across Florida, including Port St. Lucie, are already building the potential loss into their budget planning. Lucie County homeowners currently pay the highest property tax in the state, according to Florida tax data. Scott Samples with the city said the council will reconvene shortly after the November 3rd election to determine next steps, whether the proposal is passed or fails.

cards.headline: P1 Motor Club private racetrack resort breaks ground in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: A new private racetrack resort community is under construction on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits and welcoming its first drivers this fall.
cards.body:
P1 Motor Club features racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts. The club is designed for drivers of all ages and skill levels, welcoming children as young as 8 years old driving go-karts. Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members.

The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit. Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks.

Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club, said developers want to preserve the character of the region by planting trees, creating lakes, and incorporating natural landscaping throughout the property. P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.
cards.article_text: A new private racetrack resort community is under construction in St. Lucie County, replacing fairways with racing circuits and welcoming its first drivers this fall.P1 Motor Club is being built on 650 acres off Okeechobee Road, featuring 10 miles of racing circuits designed for street cars, race cars and go-karts.WATCH BELOW: Inside P1 Motor Club: St. Lucie County's new racetrack resort"Think of a high-end golf resort," said Chris DuPlessis, Director of Fun for P1 Motor Club. "Instead of a golf course, you've got a racetrack."The club is designed for drivers of all ages and skill levels."We get kids as young as 8 years old driving go-karts, all the way up to you know, grandpa comes and still drives on track in his car, so it's a family club," DuPlessis said.The first track under construction is the 3-mile Treasure Coast Track, set to open in October. Over the next six months, crews will continue work on additional circuits, including the flagship 4.5-mile P1 International Circuit.Membership comes with a $192,000 initiation fee and $12,000 in yearly dues. The club already has 260 members.Construction on a clubhouse and homes for up to 125 residents is scheduled to begin in 2027. The development will also include condos and customizable garages with living spaces situated directly along the tracks.Despite the scale of the project, developers say they want to preserve the character of the region by planting trees, creating lakes, and incorporating natural landscaping throughout the property."It'll feel like it's been a racetrack here for 100 years," DuPlessis said. "It's like we're building a city, and if you couldn't tell, we're quite excited about it."P1 Motor Club is expected to be fully completed by 2028.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.
